title: The Shape of a Pause / 停顿的形状
input_provenance: AI-generated original fictional botanical studio photograph.
pipeline: Generate a photographic input; inspect it; edit that exact image into an imprint; refine the resulting artwork once to replace pencil hatching with softer broken transfer impressions.

before.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create one sophisticated original botanical still-life photograph of exactly two dark wine-red calla lilies, one tall and one lower, with long naturally curved stems and exactly one broad gently undulating deep-green leaf. Portrait 4:5. A spare off-axis composition with the graceful rhythm of two elongated stems: they rise from the lower edge slightly left of center, the taller flower curves toward the upper-right quadrant, and the shorter flower opens at mid-height toward the left. Their heights and facing directions differ. The stems approach each other gently without becoming parallel or symmetrical. A single broad leaf folds quietly behind the lower stem, providing one soft green counterweight, not a bouquet. Preserve the anatomically correct elegant rolled funnel-like spathes, clean thin curled rims, smooth sweeping surfaces, and small visible warm ochre spadices. The tall flower has a long beautifully tapered point and a generous open curve; the lower one is more turned, showing an elegant rolled side. Both are fresh and alive, not wilted. Flowers and stems occupy a poised diagonal through the composition with generous quiet negative space and no crowded edges. Stem bases continue naturally out of the bottom crop; no vase needs to be visible.

Background: seamless pale warm-grey studio background with a very gentle natural falloff, no horizon or texture. Lighting: broad soft directional daylight from upper left, grazing the rolled flower edges, revealing a rich range from muted deep burgundy to velvety wine-red in the petal folds. True realistic matte plant surfaces, subtle delicate veins only on close inspection, green stems softly lit, restrained highlights, no lacquer-like gloss. The photograph should be tactile, quiet, sculptural, emotionally composed, with controlled organic asymmetry and beautiful flowing contours. Rich colors but no over-saturation. Shot like a contemporary fine-art botanical photograph, not a wedding arrangement or catalog cutout. No other flowers, extra leaves, ribbon, hands, vase, ornaments, water droplets, props, text, border, signature or watermark. Not an illustration or 3D render. This will serve as an AI-generated source image for a real follow-up image-to-imprint transformation.

after.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Edit the supplied calla-lily photograph into a refined Soul Imprint / 灵魂拓印 artwork on fresh luminous white paper. Use this exact photograph as the source, preserving its portrait 4:5 framing, the precise two flower silhouettes and facing directions, heights, long curved stems, their point of convergence, the single broad undulating leaf and the open negative space. There are exactly two blooms and one leaf. Do not redesign the arrangement, duplicate parts, make it symmetrical, shorten the stems, crop the top tip or move the flowers.

Translate the flowers into selective, tactile graphite impressions, with graceful sustained curves and large beautiful unprinted areas. This version should be especially elegant and spacious. At the taller upper-right bloom, a few distinct dark-grey impressions follow short portions of the rolled lower lip, the tapered outer tip and the central spadix. Very soft, restrained transfer fragments close to those folds suggest the curled funnel shape, but most of the broad spathe is clean untouched white paper. The shorter left bloom is treated similarly, with its curling left tip and forward lower rim supplying a quiet counter-rhythm. Keep the distinctive flow of each flower readable through a few connected fragments, with stretches of their perimeters missing. Do not outline the flowers completely and do not shade or fill their entire petals. Preserve white expanses within the flowers as well as outside them.

The two long stems are slender, flowing charcoal-grey-to-silver-grey traces with controlled interruptions, retaining their exact natural curvature and connection to the blooms. Avoid drawing perfectly continuous contour pairs all the way down each stem. The single broad leaf becomes much lighter: a sparse broken midrib and a small number of gently directional deposits along portions of its curled edge, with most of its interior absent. Keep it secondary. Let the image be led by the two flower curves and the long stem rhythm. Texture should be localized, finely dry and soft at its edges, with a few convincing pressure changes. No dense confetti of fragments, peppery full-page noise, harsh chips, scratchy scribbles or busy veins. Not a complete pencil sketch made pale, not a greyscale photograph, not a black silhouette, not vector outline art. No regular hatching or realistic continuous volume shading. The image is a selective material trace, with information intentionally withheld.

Neutral-to-slightly-cool white thin paper fills the frame, with only extremely fine fibers visible close up. No beige or aged paper, no full-page creases, no stains, no decoratively worn border. A couple of subtle pressure variations on the paper can appear very locally but must not clutter the white field. Replace the photographic grey background entirely with clean white paper. Monochrome graphite only. Keep the design alive, lyrical, measured and materially delicate, with enough firmness in the flower folds and hearts to hold attention at thumbnail size. No words, title, numbers, signature, frame, vase, added foliage, hands, tools or before/after panel. Deliver one full-frame finished art image.
after.refinement_prompt:
Refine this existing calla-lily imprint artwork with one targeted change in mark-making only. Keep the exact two flower shapes, positions, sizes, stem curves, leaf, framing and beautiful large white petal interiors. Preserve the elegant flowing rhythm, delicate tonal balance, crisp spadices and the dark rolled petal folds. Do not rearrange or add anything.

Replace the visible longitudinal pencil-hatching and hand-drawn contour texture with soft dry graphite-transfer deposits: small pressure patches, subtly granular but coherent impressions, clean little interruptions where a rubbing failed to print. The rolled front lip of each calla should read as a softly deposited narrow band, with a few small unprinted breaks and a clearly more solid pressure point, not repeated pencil strokes. At the upper flower's outer rim, leave some short sections entirely absent while retaining the tapered tip. On each stem, replace doubled continuous drawn lines with a slim irregular pressure trace, allowing two or three short areas to quietly vanish into white without losing its flowing curve or connection to the bloom. On the leaf keep only the most necessary sparse impressions. Avoid scratchiness, scattered confetti, erosion craters, coarse dirt, dark blotches or over-distressing. Keep the image clean and lyrical. Fresh neutral-white paper, graphite grey, no words, no yellowing, no extra texture, no framing. The result should feel delicately transferred or rubbed, with the same refined silhouette and clear breathing room as the input.

quality_review: Both input and final result visually inspected. The two differently oriented calla blooms, one broad leaf, and long curved stems retain their arrangement. Wide white petal interiors, restrained dark spadices and rolled rims create the intended graceful line rhythm. One targeted refinement reduced pencil-like continuous strokes and interrupted stem marks. This is an AI-generated showcase, not a physical rubbing.
